data.name: Khisb
data.gender_notes: Khisb is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Khisb is derived from the Arabic root kh-s-b, which means 'to eat' or 'food'. In Islamic tradition, Khisb refers to a type of food, usually grains or cereals, that is distributed to the needy during the month of Ramadan. This act of giving and sharing is considered an act of charity and righteousness. The name Khisb carries the meaning “A type of food” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Khisb usually hope their child will grow to embody a type of food and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Khisb belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “A type of food.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Khisb total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The practice of distributing Khisb during Ramadan is deeply rooted in the Islamic culture and tradition. It is an expression of the communal spirit of the month and a symbol of solidarity with the less fortunate members of society. In many Muslim communities, the collection and distribution of Khisb is organized through local mosques and community centers. It is not uncommon for families and individuals to set aside a portion of their own food supplies to contribute to this cause.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the act of giving and sharing Khisb is considered an act of sacrifice and service to Allah. Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is reported to have said, "Whoever gives food to a fasting person to break his fast, Allah will save him from the Fire." (Sahih Muslim). By contributing to the Khisb, one not only helps to alleviate the physical hardships of the needy but also contributes to their spiritual upliftment by providing them with the opportunity to fast and offer their own prayers during Ramadan. In this way, the act of giving Khisb reflects the essence of Islamic values of generosity, compassion, and unity among believers.
